The continuity facts the finding cites do not erase the close: the four-token flight core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר collates byte at oshb:Isa.2.10 and accent_stripped at oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 1 verse byte, 3 verses accent_stripped), and the idols lexeme stands at oshb:Isa.2.8, oshb:Isa.2.18 and oshb:Isa.2.20 (אֱלִילִ֑ים, אֱלִילֵ֣י, byte tier; sweep: 8 verses skeleton book-wide, 3 in this chapter) — both motifs bind 2:18-22 to the FIRST stanza (2:5-11) across the whole of 2:12-17, so they straddle the 2:11 refrain close exactly as they straddle the 2:17 one; they argue the poem-level envelope over 2:5-22 that the neighbour row already discloses as a rival, not a merger of 2:18-22 with 2:12-17. The seam is therefore warranted from BOTH sides by byte-true ruled signals that the row itself already splices and cites — which is why the finding and the prior adjudication agree the placement is not the defect. The row's load-bearing clause is two-part: (i) a frame-mode shift 'at MT 7:18 itself' — byte-true at the seam (three 2ms suffixes at 7:17 against none at 7:18; a narrated scene with a named addressee giving way to an unaddressed announcement); (ii) a cycle-wide generalisation that 7:18-25 'names no speaker and addresses no one directly'. 'Addresses no one directly' is byte-OPEN, not byte-false: the sole candidate is תָב֣וֹא inside לֹֽא תָב֣וֹא שָׁ֔מָּה יִרְאַ֖ת שָׁמִ֣יר וָשָׁ֑יִת (oshb:Isa.7.25, byte tier), a qal imperfect whose 2ms and 3fs forms are identical in the pointed bytes; no morphology layer is staged, so the parse cannot be machine-settled, and the 3fs parse — the feminine construct noun that follows as its subject, 'the fear of briers and thorns shall not come there' — is byte-available and is paralleled by יָ֣בוֹא שָׁ֑מָּה in the preceding verse (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier), the third-person 'one comes there'. The row's own second witness renders it second person — “you shall not come there for fear of briers and thorns;” (web:Isa.7.25) — while rendering the cycle's two other taw-prefixed forms, תִּסְפֶּֽה (oshb:Isa.7.20, byte tier) and תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה (oshb:Isa.7.24, byte tier), as third person; the row quotes that rendering and neither argues the parse nor reconciles it. Under the tier-disclosure standard a form-class claim is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses; as shipped the clause is unsupported and witness-contradicted, and against the facing row's 'addressed to the same audience' / 'the four share one addressee' (where 'addressee' means the oracle's target, not a grammatical addressee) the two rows are terminologically inconsistent. The prior adjudication applied the byte-false-load-bearing-warrant rule, testing the characterisation at the cycle's far end (7:25) and treating the demoted formula as if absent; on the complete test the load-bearing kernel (the shift at the seam) is byte-true, sound warrants stand on both sides in the row's own splices, and the defective part is an over-extended, unargued generalisation plus the row's inverted ordering ('cannot discriminate the cut on its own' — a first-site formula onset does discriminate: nothing of the class stands at oshb:Isa.7.17). A defective load-bearing warrant over a byte-sound, twice-warranted seam is the medium class of this queue (defective warrant, boundary uncontested), not high. Downgrade to medium. Cure as proposed, no span change: delete the 'addresses no one directly' clause, re-argue the rear seam from the 7:17 second-person close and the 7:18 formula onset with the PE as tier-3 corroboration, and align the two rows' 'addressee' wording.

The finding's remaining ground ('no vocative, imperative onset, messenger frame, wayyiqtol onset or addressee change stands at MT 61:4') was onset-only, so per the re-adjudication instruction the seam was re-ruled on the complete both-sides test. Side (a), the row's own first verse: וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) carries no vocative, no imperative, no divine-speech, massa or hoy frame (the device inventory's koh-amar 48-verse, neum 23-verse, amar-YHWH-adjacency 52-verse, massa and hoy censuses key 0 sites in MT ch 61), and no addressee shift, the unit's second-person-plural address first appearing at צֹאנְכֶ֑ם (oshb:Isa.61.5, byte tier) and וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier): no ruled tier-1 onset. Side (b), the preceding unit's last verse, weighed under the refrain-close rule: 61:3's closing word לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) byte-recurs at exactly one other site, לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier; sweep: 2 verses book-wide on the pointed form), where it closes a verse inside the preceding unit rather than that unit's close, which falls at 60:22 on the divine self-identification אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.60.22, byte tier); and its paired planting noun is not byte-shared, the 60:21 ketiv/qere pair נֵ֧צֶר מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier; a K/Q verse in the inventory, checked before slicing) meeting 61:3's מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) only at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses on that consonantal string, 14:19 included). One non-terminal recurrence with a tier-mixed partner shows no bracket function, so 'refrains close units' does not warrant 61:3 as a close, and no closing formula stands there (neum and amar-YHWH censuses: 0 sites in MT ch 61). Result of the complete test: no ruled tier-1 signal on either side of 61:3|61:4. The seam's only available warrant is the frame-scope close the finding's repair names, and the bytes support it at verse granularity with a qualification the repair must carry: the first-person commission opens at ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) with אֹתִ֜י and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier); its purpose-infinitive chain runs through לָשׂ֣וּם and לָתֵת֩ לָהֶ֨ם (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier); the turn to the waw-plus-perfect result chain happens inside 61:3 at וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier); and וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) continues that chain with an unexpressed third-person-plural subject whose nearest antecedent is 61:3's own plural pronoun (whole-token consonantal count of that pronoun in MT 61:1-9: 4 tokens, 61:3 twice, 61:7 לָהֶֽם and 61:8 אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם, byte tier, none in 61:1-2). So 61:3|61:4 is the first verse boundary after the frame's governed chain is exhausted, and no clause spans it: 61:3 ends a complete clause closed by its own purpose infinitive, so the one-sentence rule (a syntactically continuous sentence spanning verses is one unit) does not bind, and 61:4 opens a new clause with its own object. The replacement warrant therefore passes the discrimination test that killed the original only when stated as a frame-scope close, never as a construction contrast, and it must disclose the cross-seam continuity it survives: the waw-plus-perfect chain and the plural referent run across the seam; the first-person-plural לֵאלֹהֵ֑ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.2, byte tier) recurs as אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier; sweep: 14 verses book-wide on the consonantal string, these two the only chapter-61 sites), placing the speaker's self-inclusive voice on both sides; and the first person at כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier; וְנָתַתִּ֤י, אֶכְר֥וֹת לָהֶֽם) is YHWH's own voice, a distinct object from the anointed speaker's (the self-identification's consonantal string: sweep 22 verses, 60:22 and 61:8 included; the 61:8 pointed form byte-recurs in 9 verses). Tier-3, single witness: SAMEKH keyed at 60:22 and 61:9, a count-only paseq at 61:3, no seg at 61:4; absence is never counterevidence and nothing in that layer drives this ruling; the sentence break the translation prints before “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4) is translation punctuation and drives nothing. Prior adjudication: it confirmed medium on the frame-scope ground without running the refrain-close test on 61:3; the complete test returns the same outcome, so the verdict is unchanged, but its 'nothing in 61:4-61:9 resumes that voice' needs the qualifications above (the shared plural referent and the first-person-plural form on both sides). Governing rule: a front seam is warranted by a ruled tier-1 onset in the row's first verse or a ruled tier-1 close, refrain-close under the strategy, in the preceding unit's last verse; neither is present, and the seam survives on a frame-scope close the row never states: a warrant defect, not a disclosure gap (low) and not an unwarranted seam (high), because the frame-scope close is byte-supportable at verse granularity and the row's rear seam at 61:10, שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier, a new first-person voice), is untouched. Confirm at the filed medium; the field repair stands with no seam movement: state the frame-scope close against MT 61:3's bytes, add oshb:Isa.61.3 and web:Isa.61.3 to boundary_evidence_refs, re-cut rejected_alternative to the rival the bytes actually pose (61:4-61:9 read as the continuation of the commission speech of 61:1-61:3, grounded in the shared waw-plus-perfect chain and plural referent), and treat observed_substrate_signals and confidence as dependent fields. Coherence with the preceding row's side of the same seam: its 'changed subject' reason is not byte-discriminating either, since 61:4 names no new subject, so the pair's shared seam rests on the one frame-scope close and both rows' repairs are one edit.
